title: Babenbergs receive the March of Austria
description: Emperor Otto II gives the eastern march on the Danube to Leopold I, whose Babenberg family rules it until 1246.

title: First record of the name Austria
description: A deed of Emperor Otto III uses the name Ostarrîchi for the region, the oldest known form of Österreich.

title: Austria becomes a duchy
description: By the Privilegium Minus, Emperor Frederick Barbarossa raises Austria from a march to a duchy independent of Bavaria.

title: Battle on the Marchfeld
description: Rudolf of Habsburg defeats and kills Ottokar II of Bohemia, and Austria passes to the Habsburgs, who hold it until 1918.

title: Habsburgs gain Bohemia and Hungary
description: After Louis II dies at Mohács, Ferdinand of Austria is elected king of Bohemia and claims Hungary, joining the three lands under one ruler.

title: Pragmatic Sanction
description: Charles VI decrees that the Habsburg lands may not be divided and may pass to a daughter.

title: Maria Theresa succeeds
description: On the death of Charles VI his daughter inherits the Habsburg lands, and Prussia's seizure of Silesia begins the War of the Austrian Succession.

title: Austrian Empire proclaimed
description: Francis II takes the title Emperor of Austria, two years before the Holy Roman Empire is dissolved.

title: Battle of Austerlitz
description: Napoleon defeats the Austrian and Russian armies, forcing Austria out of the Third Coalition.

title: Congress of Vienna concludes
description: The Final Act redraws the map of Europe after Napoleon, with Austria presiding over the new German Confederation.

title: Revolution in Vienna
description: Crowds force the resignation of Chancellor Metternich, and revolts follow across the empire.

title: Battle of Königgrätz
description: Prussia defeats Austria in the decisive battle of their seven-week war, ending Austrian leadership in Germany.

title: Austro-Hungarian Compromise
description: The empire is divided into Austrian and Hungarian halves under one monarch, with shared foreign policy and army.

title: Assassination of Franz Ferdinand
description: Gavrilo Princip shoots the heir to the throne and his wife, setting off the crisis that leads to the First World War.

title: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
description: A month after Sarajevo the declaration of war draws in Russia, Germany, France and Britain within a week.

title: Republic of German-Austria proclaimed
description: The day after Emperor Charles I gives up his part in government, the provisional assembly declares a republic.

title: Treaty of Saint-Germain
description: The peace treaty confirms the break-up of the empire and forbids union with Germany.

title: Austrian Civil War
description: Four days of fighting between the socialist militia and government forces end with the Social Democrats banned.

title: Dollfuss assassinated
description: Austrian Nazis kill Chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss in a failed coup.

title: Anschluss
description: German troops cross the border and Austria is annexed to Germany the next day.

title: Second Republic declared
description: With Vienna in Soviet hands, a provisional government under Karl Renner declares Austria independent of Germany.

title: Austrian State Treaty
description: The four occupying powers restore Austria's sovereignty, and their troops leave by October.

title: Declaration of Neutrality
description: Parliament passes a constitutional law declaring permanent neutrality; the date is now the national day.

title: Austria joins the European Union
description: Austria becomes a member together with Finland and Sweden.
